calibrated_on: ubuntu-latest (GitHub Actions), Ruby 4.0.7, rbs 4.2.0, release-gate-frozen-corpus @ run 38835348158
note: Linux CI measurements of the v0.4.4 release candidate's engine (release/0.4.4 @ 94041d524) over the same frozen corpus v0.4.3, recalibrated during the v0.4.4 release prep (2026-10-16) on the maintainer's ruling after the release gate read allocations just past the band. The previous baseline (run 38742170801, the v0.4.3 engine) read 53,739,536 allocations, wall_s 65.183, peak_rss_kb 533,164; this run (38835348158) reads 54,837,910 allocations (+1,098,374, +2.04% against a +2% band), wall_s 62.658, peak_rss_kb 535,936. Attribution: Ruby 4.0.7 and rbs 4.2.0 are unchanged and Gemfile.lock changed only in its own version line, so the rise is engine cost from the PRs merged since v0.4.3. Their Engine allocations A/B on this corpus: #1965 +749,546 (+1.36%, above the 1.0% warning band, the self-call instance-variable write analysis; the warning went unanswered on the PR and is accepted by this ruling), #1932 +176,462 (+0.33%), #1961 +144,468 (+0.26%), #1928 +41,946 (+0.08%), and every other PR within +/-3,000; #1917, #1952, #1970, #1976 and #1981 left no delta in their job logs. Those deltas sum to about 1.12M, which accounts for the rise. The band is a budget for the engine cost added since this calibration. Refresh on the same corpus after an engine improvement by measuring the improving PR's own merge commit, and list in the new note every per-PR warning since this calibration with its answer; an unanswered one needs the user's ruling first. A red cut clears only by attributing the rise and recalibrating on the same corpus on the user's ruling. After each release the corpus advances to the new tag. bench/README.md and the rigor-release-prep skill carry the procedures. Sampling rule (#987): each gate run takes 2 reps per target, EACH IN A FRESH PROCESS (VmHWM is a per-process high-water mark, so an in-process rep can never report lower RSS, and a warm rep's wall is not comparable with this cold baseline), and records the LOWER of the reps for wall_s and peak_rss_kb while allocations and diagnostics are taken from the first rep unreduced. Measure a recalibration the same way -- bench/baseline.updated.json is already reduced, so committing it preserves the rule.
